title: The wide permitted
hook: most of life is simply permitted

segments.voice: Yesterday, ahkam, the rulings, and your line: five kinds of acts. When you sorted three of yours, where did they land on the dial? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-seven.

The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells the people that Allah has made the pilgrimage a duty for them. A man calls out: every year, Messenger of Allah? The Prophet stays silent. The man asks again, and again. Finally the answer comes, in Sahih Muslim: if I said yes, it would become a duty every year, and you would not be able to do it. Then a request: leave me as I leave you. Don't go hunting for burdens nobody placed on you. Today's word is the space that request protects.
screen: `EVERY YEAR, MESSENGER?` → `SILENCE.` → `LEAVE ME AS I LEAVE YOU.`

segments.voice: The word is mubah, permitted, the middle of yesterday's dial. No reward for doing it, no blame for leaving it. Just allowed. And jurists have a principle about it that changes how the whole law feels: in things and in dealings, the starting point is permission. Something is permitted unless a text forbids it. Not the other way round. The Qur'an says, in Surah al-Baqarah: "He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth." For you. The food, the trade, the clothes, the games, the jokes, the long walk at dusk. Jurists start from yes, and ask for evidence before they say no. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari puts the warning sharply. The Prophet says the Muslim with the greatest guilt is the one who asks about something that wasn't forbidden, and it becomes forbidden because of his asking. Asking, in that report, isn't the problem. Inventing burdens is. Now one turn, so this isn't misread. The starting point flips for worship. Jurists say a new act of worship needs a text behind it, because worship is offered the way it was taught. So in prayer, start from what was taught. In the market and the kitchen and the park, start from permitted. Put those two together and something becomes visible. The forbidden is a list, and the permitted is a wide field. A person can spend most of a day in the field, eating, working, laughing, resting, and none of it is outside the law. Some of it can even become worship, jurists add, when it's done with a good intention.
screen: `MUBAH: SIMPLY PERMITTED.` · `THE STARTING POINT IS YES.` · `DON'T INVENT BURDENS.` · `WORSHIP STARTS FROM WHAT WAS TAUGHT.`

segments.voice: The practice: enjoy one permitted thing. Choose something small that's simply allowed. A cup of tea. Bread still warm. The sound outside your window. A stretch. Do it now, or hold it in your mind if you can't. Slowly. Don't turn it into a task or a lesson. Let it be what it is: a good thing, in the wide field, with no permission slip needed. If you pray, you can thank Allah for it. If not, just stay with the taste of it. The bell holds the time.
Mubah. Permitted: no reward for doing it, no blame for leaving it, and in things and dealings, the starting point. Today's word.
Your line: most is permitted. Today, when you catch yourself inventing a rule nobody gave you, put it down. Leave it as it was left. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-seven.

howItsDone: Muslim jurists generally start from permission in food, trade and everyday life, asking for evidence before calling something forbidden, while acts of worship follow what was taught.

original.note: Arabic: permitted, allowed; the middle of the five rulings.

trapdoor: what you thought: a religious law tells you what you're allowed to do.
what it means: in things and dealings, everything starts permitted, and only a text can forbid.
what a scholar hears: al-asl fi al-ashya' al-ibahah, the default in things is permission; and its reverse in worship.

notes: Muslim 1337: confirm number and paraphrase; the text says the man asked three times; the script says 'again, and again'.
Qur'an 2:29 quoted from Pickthall 1930: confirm exact wording.
Bukhari 7289: confirm number; paraphrased as 'the Muslim who wrongs the Muslims most' (a superlative the report itself uses); confirm.
Principle al-asl fi al-ashya' al-ibahah and its reverse in 'ibadat: framed as what 'jurists' say; there are minority views on the default before revelation. Confirm phrasing.
Index hook says 'most of life is simply permitted' (kept in the carry); the script avoids stating a proportion as fact.
Editor pass: Bukhari 7289 paraphrase brought closer to the report ('greatest guilt'); cut the editorial 'like a sigh' and the unsourced 'short list'.
